/-!
# Erdős Problem 947

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/947](https://www.erdosproblems.com/947)
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory
  day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [Er50] Erdős, P., *On integers of the form $2^k+p$ and some related problems*. Summa Brasil.
  Math. (1950), 113-123.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Function

namespace Erdos947

/--
There is no exact covering system - that is, a finite collection of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ with distinct $n_i$ such that every integer satisfies exactly one of these
congruence classes.

This is true, and was proved independently by Mirsky and Newman and by Davenport and Rado; the
Mirsky–Newman proof first appeared in [Er50]. See also [Er77c].

A `StrictCoveringSystem ℤ` is a finite family of congruence classes with distinct moduli
$n_i \geq 2$ covering $\mathbb{Z}$; the trivial exact covering system consisting of the single
class $0 \pmod 1$ is therefore excluded.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos947.lean#L277"]
theorem erdos_947 : ¬ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, Pairwise (Disjoint on c.coset) := by
  sorry

end Erdos947

findings.description: The theorem docstring says the Mirsky–Newman proof "first appeared in [Er50]". The module docstring defines [Er50] as Erdős, *On integers of the form 2^k+p and some related problems*, Summa Brasil. Math. 2 (1950), 113–123. That paper does not contain the proof: its full text (pp. 113–123, footnotes included) never mentions Mirsky, Newman, Rado, or covering the integers exactly once. Its only passage on covering systems (pp. 119–120) gives two coverings with distinct moduli: {0(2), 0(3), 1(4), 5(6), 7(12)} and a 14-congruence system whose least modulus is 3. It then conjectures that the minimum modulus can be arbitrarily large. The Mirsky–Newman proof (a generating-function argument with z → e^{2πi/n_k}) is presented in Erdős's 1952 Hungarian paper in Mat. Lapok, pp. 122–128 (proof on p. 126). The Lean statement itself is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: Er50, full OCR text from users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1950-07.pdf, p. 119: "The simplest system of congruences a_i (mod n_i), n_1 < n_2 < ... < n_k so that every integer satisfies at least one of them is: 0 (mod 2), 0 (mod 3), 1 (mod 4), 5 (mod 6), 7 (mod 12) ... Davenport found a slightly more complicated system somewhat earlier. It seems likely that for every c there exists such a system all the moduli of which are > c." Nothing about exactness or Mirsky–Newman appears anywhere in the paper. Erdős, "Egy kongruenciarendszerekről szóló problémáról" [On a problem concerning congruence systems], Mat. Lapok (1952), 122–128 (users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1952-03.pdf): "sejtettem ... vagyis a rendszer nem egyszeresen fedi le az egész számokat. Ezt azonban nem tudtam bebizonyítani. (8)-ra MIRSKY és NEWMANN a következő szellemes bizonyítást találta (ugyanezt a bizonyítást találta később DAVENPORT és RADÓ is)", i.e. "I conjectured ... that the system does not cover the integers exactly once, but I could not prove it; Mirsky and Newman found the following ingenious proof of (8) (Davenport and Radó later found the same proof)". erdosproblems.com/947 cites only [Er77c] and makes no [Er50] claim.
findings.suggested_fix: In the theorem docstring, either drop the clause "the Mirsky–Newman proof first appeared in [Er50]" or cite the 1952 paper instead: Erdős, P., *Egy kongruenciarendszerekről szóló problémáról* (On a problem concerning congruence systems), Mat. Lapok (1952), 122–128. Update the module reference list to match.

reformulations.difference: The source (erdosproblems.com/947) says there is no finite collection of classes a_i (mod n_i) with distinct n_i such that every integer satisfies exactly one of them. Read literally, the trivial one-class system {0 mod 1} is a counterexample, so the source implicitly excludes it. The Lean differs in three ways. (1) Moduli are ideals of ℤ, and distinctness means `moduli` is injective. (2) The trivial system is excluded by requiring every modulus to be neither ⊥ nor ⊤, i.e. n_i ≥ 2 (`ne_bot`, `ne_top`), rather than by saying "other than the trivial system". (3) "Exactly one" is split into covering (`unionCovers`) plus `Pairwise (Disjoint on c.coset)`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An exact covering that contains a class mod 1 consists of that class alone: any other class a_j (mod n_j) would meet it at a_j. So requiring n_i ≥ 2 excludes exactly the trivial system, and a single class mod n ≥ 2 never covers ℤ. Every nonzero ideal of ℤ is (n) for a unique n > 0, and (n) = (m) iff |n| = |m|, so injective ideals means distinct moduli. Covering plus pairwise disjointness is "every integer in exactly one class". This matches Erdős's own formulation in Mat. Lapok 1952 ("x ≡ a_i (mod n_i), 1 < n_1 < n_2 < … < n_k") and Wikipedia's "distinct (moduli different and bigger than 1)" and "disjoint". I proved the equivalence in Lean with only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The proved statement is `(¬ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, Pairwise (Disjoint on c.coset)) ↔ ∀ k (a : Fin k → ℤ) (n : Fin k → ℕ), (∀ i, 0 < n i) → Injective n → (∀ z : ℤ, ∃! i, z ≡ a i [ZMOD n i]) → k = 1` (file /workspace/review/equiv.lean). I also derived the file's exact statement from the linked formal proof, which compiles here (file /workspace/review/combined.lean).

review.notes:
The file has one declaration, Erdos947.erdos_947. Its mathematics is correct.

- **Status matches the source.** erdosproblems.com/947 says "PROVED (LEAN): solved in the affirmative". The file has `research solved`, and its `formal_proof` link points to the right theorem (line 277 of the plby file is `theorem erdos_947`).
- **The linked proof checks out.** It compiles against this sandbox's Mathlib (v4.33.1) using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. From it I derived the file's exact statement `¬ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, Pairwise (Disjoint on c.coset)` in /workspace/review/combined.lean.
- **The statement is not vacuous.**
  - Erdős's covering {0(2), 0(3), 1(4), 5(6), 7(12)} builds as a `StrictCoveringSystem ℤ`, and its classes are not pairwise disjoint.
  - {0(2), 1(2)} builds as a `CoveringSystem ℤ` with pairwise disjoint classes, but not a strict one.
  - So the claim really depends on distinct moduli together with exactness (/workspace/review/scratch3.lean).
- **Er77c p. 48 was not read.** The Rényi archive links "Problems and results on combinatorial number theory III" to 1976-34.pdf, which is actually a different paper. This affects only the "See also [Er77c]" citation, which erdosproblems.com itself also uses.
- **The only finding is a minor docstring reference slip:** the [Er50] attribution. It does not affect the Lean statement.
